brief.question: Are published spiking-GNN accuracies commensurable across papers, and what makes a reported number portable?
brief.answer: No: an executable audit of every code-releasing method in a bounded seven-method survey finds dataset-dependent reproduction failure, split-flag sensitivity worth 10.7 pp, and unlabelled split mixing in comparison tables; the binding property is split transportability, which dominates seed noise on Cora (61.5x s.d.), is marginal on CiteSeer (4.1x), and is confounded on PubMed (2.2x).
brief.audience: Benchmark/evaluation researchers and practitioners assembling spiking-GNN comparison tables.
brief.domain_bridge: A number measured under one split is not a baseline for another; the audit makes the split label and the reproduction environment part of the claim.
priorities: unlabelled split mixing as a field-level hazard

terminology.transportability: split gap vs measured seed spread

facts.statement: Three of seven surveyed methods ship code and form the auditable census; SpikingGCN reproduces on CiteSeer (70.6 vs 72.5) but fails dataset-dependently elsewhere (Cora 50.0 vs 80.7, 5 seeds, per-seed 0.481-0.526; PubMed 64.3 vs 77.6, 3 seeds, s.d. 5.37 pp).
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact

facts.statement: SpikeGraphormer reproduces on its own split (84.7 vs 84.8 plus/minus 0.7, 3 runs) and drops to 74.0 on the public split: one flag is worth 10.7 pp.
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact

facts.statement: Comparison tables quote the same baseline on two splits without labels: one paper GCN row 81.5 is consistent with the Split-I family; another SpikingGCN row 87.7/77.7/87.5 is consistent with Split II (88.7/77.6/89.3); split definitions quoted verbatim (arXiv:2205.02767).
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact

facts.statement: Input conventions decide the SpikingGCN Cora cell: raw bag-of-words 51.5% with or without self-loops; every row-normalised variant collapses to 13.0% including the conventional max-rescale fix; the old fourth-row 13.0 was the row-normalised no-self-loop variant (mislabel corrected).
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact

facts.statement: Split transportability vs matching seed noise, per dataset: Cora gap 8.0 pp = 4.06x SpikingGCN's own seed s.d. (1.97 pp, 5 seeds) = 1.35x the 3sigma bar (marginal); CiteSeer 5.1 pp = 4.11x a labelled proxy noise (SpikeGCL 1.24 pp s.d.; matching cell single-seed) = 1.37x the bar (marginal); PubMed 11.7 pp = 2.18x its s.d. (5.37 pp) = 0.73x the bar (confounded, re-scoped). No dataset-level strong verdict stands.
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact

facts.statement: Every audit-table number recomputes from raw logs: replay/checksum audit 0 mismatches.
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact

facts.statement: A same-nominal-seed CiteSeer re-run differed by 1.0 pp from the audited cell (0.7826 vs 0.7728): recorded sensitivity evidence.
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact

facts.statement: The census covers the seven methods of this survey (three with code); no field-wide claim; this audit covers trained spiking GNNs, not training-free conversion methods.
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact

facts.statement: Each individual number is internally consistent: a variance checklist would catch none of these failures; the binding property is transportability, not variance.
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact

facts.statement: SpikingGCN's own Cora seed spread is 1.97 pp s.d. (per-seed 48.1-52.6, 5 seeds) and its PubMed spread 5.37 pp s.d. (3 seeds, derived).
facts.condition: as specified in the named artifact
